title: Converting Between Customary and Metric Units
seo_title: Grade 7 Converting Between Customary and Metric Units Worksheets (TEKS 7.4E, STAAR)
standard_text: 7.4E convert between measurement systems, including the use of proportions and the use of unit rates
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 worksheets for Texas TEKS 7.4E: convert length, mass, weight and capacity between customary and metric units with proportions and unit rates. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: To the unit with more pieces, multiply; back again, divide.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A conversion factor is a ratio, such as 1 inch : 2.54 cm.
  • To change to the unit with more pieces (inches to centimeters), multiply by the factor.
  • To change back, divide by the factor.
  • You can also set up a proportion: 1/2.54 = x/30.

Examples

Example

12 in. to centimeters (1 in. = 2.54 cm)

12 × 2.54

Answer: 30.48 cm

Example

10 km to miles (1 mi ≈ 1.6 km)

10 ÷ 1.6

Answer: 6.25 mi

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Multiplying when you should divideKilometers to miles: there are fewer miles, so divide by 1.6.
Using the wrong factorRead which unit the factor starts from.
Rounding too earlyRound only the final answer.

faq.q: Do I need to memorize the factors?
faq.a: No. Problems and the STAAR reference materials give the conversion factors.
Many factors, like 1 mile ≈ 1.6 km, are rounded.
Write the factor as a ratio and match units: 1 kg/2.2 lb = x kg/11 lb.
